summary: The observations OTLP exporter also sends account limits as a bounded gauge and the claims each node stores by kind and writer, counted as they are stored; the docs name the observation log as the full harness telemetry series

replay.detail: No claim is written or replayed differently. A trigger on claim insert adds to the node-local claim_writes totals in the same transaction; deleting claims never changes them.

schema.detail: Adds the node-local table claim_writes (kind, writer, claims, bytes), the trigger claim_writes_insert AFTER INSERT ON claims, and the meta key claim_writes_since_unix_ms, created on open with IF NOT EXISTS. They are not replicated, not part of any claim, projection or checkpoint digest, and an older build ignores them.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: A node with [observations.otlp] configured also posts to the collector's /v1/metrics: st_account_limit_used_percent (gauge; driver, account, window; the newest measured reading per window), and st_claims_stored_total and st_claim_body_bytes_stored_total (cumulative sums from claim_writes_since_unix_ms; kind, writer) whenever the totals changed. The totals count each claim as it is stored, here or received, so they stay a true write rate after local trim deletes superseded claims. A batch's cursor still moves only when every signal is accepted. Without [observations.otlp] the totals are still kept but nothing is sent. No claim kind, field, wire or CLI contract changes.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade. The table and trigger are created on open; counting starts then, with no backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting stops the gauge and the counters; the claim_writes table, its trigger and the meta key stay and keep counting until dropped, harmlessly.
